revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Choosing a Time-Capsule Box
revealWordProblem.text: Your class is choosing a box for the time capsule. The store sells three rectangular-prism boxes: a Small box that is 2 ft × 1 ft × 1 ft, a Medium box that is 2 ft × 1.5 ft × 1 ft, and a Large box that is 2 ft × 2 ft × 1.5 ft. Compute the volume of each box in cubic feet. Which box should the class buy if they need to fit at least 5 cubic feet of items? Explain how you decided.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Small: V = 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 ft³. Medium: V = 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³. Large: V = 2 × 2 × 1.5 = 6 ft³. The class should buy the Large box because only its volume, 6 ft³, is at least 5 ft³.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in?
questions.explanation: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 cubic inches.
choiceFeedback: Are you adding the dimensions? Volume multiplies all edges: length × width × height.
Not quite. V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = ___ cubic inches.
Check the units. Area is square units (²), volume is cubic units (³).
hints: Spot the three edges: l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in. Volume fills the whole box, so all three matter.
Use V = l × w × h and remember the answer needs cubic units (in³), not square units.
Multiply 4 × 3 = 12 for the base, then multiply that result by the height, 5 inches.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma rectangular con l = 4 in, w = 3 in, h = 5 in?
questions.explanationEs: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: Identifica las tres aristas: l = 4 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 5 pulg. El volumen llena toda la caja, así que las tres importan.
Usa V = l × a × h y recuerda que la respuesta necesita unidades cúbicas (pulg³), no cuadradas.
Multiplica 4 × 3 = 12 para la base y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 5 pulgadas.

choiceFeedback: That's the width from the problem, not the height — divide the volume by length × width instead.

hints: You're given the volume (36 cm³) plus two edges (6 cm and 3 cm). The height is what's missing.

questions.stemEs: Una caja tiene un volumen de 36 cm³. Su longitud es 6 cm y su ancho es 3 cm. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Te dan el volumen (36 cm³) más dos aristas (6 cm y 3 cm). Lo que falta es la altura.

questions.stem: How is volume different from area?
choices: Volume measures 3D space (cubic units); area measures 2D surface (square units)
Volume uses square units; area uses cubic units
Volume only applies to cubes; area applies to all shapes
questions.explanation: Volume measures the space inside a 3D shape (cubic units like in³). Area measures a flat 2D surface (square units like in²).
choiceFeedback: The units are swapped here — think about which measurement fills 3D space and which covers a flat surface.
Volume isn't just for cubes — it applies to any 3D shape, like prisms and pyramids too.
These two measurements are different — one covers a flat surface, and one fills a 3D space.
hints: Think dimensions: area covers a flat 2D surface, while volume fills a 3D space.
Match each measurement to its unit: flat surfaces get square units (²), filled space gets cubic units (³).
Picture a rug (flat) versus a fish tank (filled). Decide which is area and which is volume, then check each choice.
questions.stemEs: ¿En qué se diferencia el volumen del área?
questions.explanationEs: El volumen mide el espacio dentro de una figura de tres dimensiones (unidades cúbicas como in³). El área mide una superficie plana de dos dimensiones (unidades cuadradas como in²).
choicesEs: El volumen mide el espacio en 3D (unidades cúbicas); el área mide una superficie en 2D (unidades cuadradas)
El volumen usa unidades cuadradas; el área usa unidades cúbicas
El volumen solo aplica a los cubos; el área aplica a todas las figuras
hintsEs: Piensa en dimensiones: el área cubre una superficie plana 2D, mientras que el volumen llena un espacio 3D.
Une cada medida con su unidad: las superficies planas llevan unidades cuadradas (²) y el espacio lleno lleva unidades cúbicas (³).
Imagina una alfombra (plana) frente a una pecera (llena). Decide cuál es área y cuál es volumen, y luego revisa cada opción.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Volume of Rectangular Prisms is rounding a fractional edge length to the nearest whole number before multiplying, instead of using the exact fraction or decimal. For a box that is 2 ft × 1.5 ft × 1 ft, a student might round 1.5 down to 1 and compute 2 × 1 × 1 = 2 ft³, but the correct volume uses the exact edge length: 2 × 1.5 × 1 = 3 ft³ — a full cubic foot larger. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I multiply using the exact fractional or decimal edge length, or did I round it off first?'

level3.prompt: A toy company ships action figures in boxes that are 4 × 3 × 6 inches. A shipping crate is 24 × 12 × 18 inches. How many action figure boxes fit in the crate? Explain your reasoning step by step.
level3.sentenceFrame: Each toy box has a volume of ___ in³. The crate has a volume of ___ in³. I can fit ___ boxes because ___. I checked by ___.
level3.hint: Find three different factor combinations of the target volume.
hints: Two sizes matter: each toy box is 4 × 3 × 6 in and the crate is 24 × 12 × 18 in. Each crate edge is a multiple of a box edge.
Find both volumes, then divide the crate's volume by one box's volume. Check by counting rows, columns, and layers.
Start with one toy box: multiply 4 × 3 = 12, then multiply by 6. Next find the crate's volume the same way.
level3.explanation: Each toy box holds 4 × 3 × 6 = 72 in³ and the crate holds 24 × 12 × 18 = 5184 in³, so 5184 ÷ 72 = 72 boxes fit. The division comes out exact because every crate edge is a whole-number multiple of a box edge: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 across, 12 ÷ 3 = 4 deep, and 18 ÷ 6 = 3 layers, and 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 confirms it.
level3.explanationEs: Cada caja de juguete tiene 4 × 3 × 6 = 72 in³ y la caja grande tiene 24 × 12 × 18 = 5184 in³, así que caben 5184 ÷ 72 = 72 cajas. La división sale exacta porque cada lado de la caja grande es un múltiplo entero de un lado de la caja pequeña: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 a lo ancho, 12 ÷ 3 = 4 de fondo y 18 ÷ 6 = 3 capas, y 6 × 4 × 3 = 72 lo confirma.
level3.promptEs: Una juguetería envía figuras de acción en cajas de 4 × 3 × 6 pulgadas. Una caja de embarque mide 24 × 12 × 18 pulgadas. ¿Cuántas cajas de figuras caben en la caja de embarque? Explica tu razonamiento paso a paso.
hintsEs: Importan dos tamaños: cada caja de juguetes mide 4 × 3 × 6 pulg y el cajón mide 24 × 12 × 18 pulg. Cada arista del cajón es múltiplo de una arista de la caja.
Halla ambos volúmenes y luego divide el volumen del cajón entre el de una caja. Compruébalo contando filas, columnas y capas.
Empieza con una caja de juguetes: multiplica 4 × 3 = 12 y luego multiplica por 6. Después halla el volumen del cajón igual.
